expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors

expected.title: The trace map commutes with base change through the comparison transformations
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: For the diagram of equation labelled equation-base-change with f and g Tor independent, the lemma asserts that the two transformations Lg^* o Rf_* o a -> Lg^* and Rf'_* o a' o Lg^* -> Lg^* built from the trace maps agree through the base change maps beta : Lg^* o Rf_* -> Rf'_* o L(g')^* of Cohomology, Remark labelled cohomology-remark-base-change and alpha : L(g')^* o a -> a' o Lg^* of equation labelled equation-base-change-map, i.e. that the displayed square of transformations commutes (statement lines 1866-1888). After the usual abbreviation conventions the proof recalls that beta is an isomorphism and that alpha comes from the adjoint isomorphism beta^vee : g'_* o a' -> a o g_* of Lemma labelled lemma-flat-precompose-pus, and rewrites the top horizontal arrow as a three step composition through the unit and counit of the adjunction (g^*, g_*) using that their composite is the identity (proof lines 1890-1906). It then exhibits the large diagram whose two squares commute by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats, whose triangle commutes by the observation above, and whose pentagon commutes by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints (proof lines 1908-1935). Since beta and beta^vee are isomorphisms and the outside of the diagram equals Tr_f o alpha o beta, the lemma follows (proof lines 1937-1941). Identifying the top arrow with the unit-counit composition and locating the category-theoretic identity that makes the pentagon commute is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

expected.title: Isomorphism classes of torsors under an abelian sheaf are classified by first cohomology
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The statement identifies two objects that are built by completely different means: isomorphism classes of H-torsors on a site and the first cohomology group H^1(C, H) of an abelian sheaf (statement lines 292-295). The proof has to construct both directions explicitly. The first construction is a pushout followed by a boundary operator: it forms the free abelian sheaf on the torsor, its augmentation sigma, the map a from Ker(sigma) to H determined by the torsor action through h.s' = s, pushes the sequence defining Z[F] out along a, and takes the image of 1 under the connecting homomorphism (proof lines 299-333). The second is a representability argument that needs an injective embedding, the vanishing of H^1 of an injective sheaf, and the identification of the preimage of a global section of Q = I/H as a torsor (proof lines 336-356). What the author does not do is verify that the two constructions are mutually inverse; that verification is declared omitted at proof lines 358-360 and is retained verbatim in the delivered item, so the bijection itself is asserted by the author and not carried out in the printed argument.

expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs local equations that isolate each missing point even when the ambient scheme is not globally Noetherian. It glues these equations to a line bundle realizing the open complement and uses triviality of Picard groups on localized Artinian rings to extend arbitrary line bundles from that open.

expected.title: Power-series splitting of a versal object over its minimal descent ring
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof first obtains a retraction onto the minimal descent subring and proves its restriction is an automorphism. Versality then produces sections at every Artinian order, forcing the resulting power-series map to be an isomorphism. A separate smooth-descent argument proves the descended object remains versal.

expected.title: Injectivity of residue-supported modules with characteristic-zero derivation operators
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a socle-preserving embedding into a sum of injective hulls. Leibniz operators force divisibility by a parameter, and an induction on dimension then proves surjectivity on parameter torsion. This is a module classification from differential-operator structure with a complete divisibility argument.

expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a compatible two-parameter grid of lifts through square-zero fibre-product surjections. A diagonal inverse limit produces the lift, and a quantitative power estimate proves continuity; ordinary formal smoothness alone does not directly supply these compatible topological lifts.
